newsitem.title: USA: Intel weighs down techs, Nasdaq shows slim gain.
newsitem.headline: Intel weighs down techs, Nasdaq shows slim gain.

text.p: A drop in Intel Corp overshadowed the over-the-counter market Thursday, with Nasdaq shares posting only slim gains, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index gained 3.48 points or 0.25 percent to 1411.33, a lackluster gain compared the Dow industrials, which surged 135 points or 1.79 percent to 7711.

Intel Corp, the most active Nasdaq issue, dropped 3-27/32 to 143-21/32 after Cowen & Co downgraded the stock and Goldman Sachs trimmed 1997 profit estimates. Intel said Thursday it will pass along savings from manufacturing efficiencies on its MMX-based processors to PC makers.
"Intel weighed down all the technology stocks. The rest of the semiconductor stocks got hit and the techs overall were just sloppy," said Brian Finnerty, senior vice president of Unterberg Harris.

The Philadelphia Stock Exchange semiconductor index lost 4.13 points or 1.41 percent to 287.96. But despite softness throughout the technology sector, small capitalization stocks held firm, traders said. The Russell 2000 index, a key barometer of smaller issues, gained 1.92 points to hit a new high of 389.54. Overall, advancing issues beat decliners on a margin of 11 to 10 on with 639 million shares traded.
